title: Patentability — novelty
summary: Novelty asks whether the relevant invention is new relative to prior art. A structured prior-art search is important.
source: Indian Patents Act / applicable patent framework

title: Inventive step
summary: Inventive-step analysis considers whether the claimed invention involves a technical advance or economic significance and is not obvious to a skilled person, as applicable.

title: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) pointer
summary: TKDL is relevant to traditional medicinal knowledge and prior-art context. Production systems should use authoritative access and current metadata.
source: TKDL / CSIR and Government of India resources

title: Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS)
summary: Biological-resource and associated traditional-knowledge use can trigger access-and-benefit-sharing considerations depending on the applicable framework and circumstances.

title: Nagoya Protocol
summary: The Nagoya Protocol is an international framework concerning access to genetic resources and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilization.
source: Convention on Biological Diversity — Nagoya Protocol

title: TRIPS
summary: TRIPS sets multilateral minimum standards for several categories of intellectual property protection.

title: PCT
summary: The Patent Cooperation Treaty provides an international application route that can simplify filing strategy across multiple jurisdictions; it does not itself grant a worldwide patent.

title: Madrid System
summary: The Madrid System provides a centralized mechanism for seeking trademark protection in multiple participating jurisdictions.

title: Hague System
summary: The Hague System supports international registration of industrial designs in participating jurisdictions.

title: Budapest Treaty
summary: The Budapest Treaty concerns recognition of the deposit of microorganisms for patent procedure purposes by contracting states.
